review.translation: [Then in|0] [the second|1] [month|0], [on the|2] [twenty|3]-[seventh|2] [day|4] [of the month|5], [the earth|7] [was dry|6].

analysis.evidence: הַשֵּׁנִי modifies חֹדֶשׁ to give “the second month.” The verse then specifies the twenty-seventh day of that month, confirming the calendar sense.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ + preposition בְּ־ with the definite article (בַ־) + masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In וּבַחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי, the adjective agrees with חֹדֶשׁ in gender, number, and definiteness. It identifies the second month, whose twenty-seventh day the verse then specifies.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute ordinal adjective.

analysis.evidence: שִׁבְעָה combines with וְעֶשְׂרִים ‘and twenty’ to count יוֹם ‘day’. The masculine form agrees with יוֹם, and the prefixed בְּ־ marks the date on which the earth dried, the twenty-seventh day of the second month.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ־ ‘on’ prefixed to שִׁבְעָה, a masculine singular cardinal numeral in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: In בְּשִׁבְעָה וְעֶשְׂרִים יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ, וְ joins seven and twenty to give the date, the twenty-seventh day of the month.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: In בְּשִׁבְעָה וְעֶשְׂרִים יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ, the numeral twenty-seven counts days. The phrase dates the drying of the earth to the twenty-seventh day of the second month.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse identifies the second month. In בְּשִׁבְעָה וְעֶשְׂרִים יוֹם לַחֹדֶשׁ, the marked word relates the twenty-seventh day to that month.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute noun with prefixed preposition לְ and definite article הַ, combined as לַ.

analysis.evidence: יָבְשָׁה agrees with its feminine singular subject הָאָרֶץ, “the earth.” The opening date tells when the earth had dried out.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person feminine singular

analysis.evidence: In יָבְשָׁה הָאָרֶץ, “the ground had dried,” הָאָרֶץ is the subject of the feminine singular verb יָבְשָׁה. The verse dates the drying of the ground after the flood.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute. The noun takes feminine agreement here.
